links.outcome: False positives and anatomically invalid kidney segmentations with reasoning-based rejection versus LCCA
links.effect: Reasoning-based approaches (FMR, AR, LCCAPS) reduced false positives and anatomically invalid outputs more than LCCA while preserving acceptance of valid candidates; results persisted under noise. No numbers in abstract.
links.quote: Reasoning-based approaches (FMR, AR, and LCCAPS) reduced false positives and anatomically invalid outputs more effectively than LCCA, while preserving acceptance of valid segmentation candidates.

links.outcome: Automated plausibility checks rejecting implausible segmentation outputs, including under added noise
links.effect: Reasoning-based selective acceptance reduced anatomically invalid outputs versus LCCA and avoided acceptance of implausible results under noise. No numbers in abstract.
links.quote: Results persisted under noise, avoiding acceptance of implausible results.
